literal: [8] When the emperor first expanded into the Central Plains, he paid careful attention to comfort and recruitment; for scholar-officials who came to the army gate, whether young or old, all were led in, granted audience, questioned thoroughly with full courtesy, each man could exhaust his ability, and if there was slight talent, all received appointment and use.
idiomatic: [8] As he first opened the Central Plains, the emperor welcomed every scholar who came to his camp, young or old alike, heard them out, and employed any man of even modest talent.

literal: On day jiwei, ordered Assistant State General Xi Mu to seize territory in Jinchuan, capturing Murong Bao's Prince of Danyang Maide and others at Pingtao City.
idiomatic: On the jiwei day he ordered the Assistant State General Xi Mu into Jinchuan and took Murong Bao's Prince of Danyang Maide and others at Pingtao.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day yiyou: the imperial carriage exited Jingxing Pass, sent Champion General Wang Jian and Left Army General Li Li with fifty thousand cavalry as vanguard to open the march.
idiomatic: On the yiyou day of the tenth month of winter the court passed Jingxing and sent Wang Jian and Li Li ahead with fifty thousand horse.

literal: Eleventh month, day gengzi on the new moon: the emperor reached Zhending.
idiomatic: On the new moon of the eleventh month, the gengzi day, he reached Zhending.

literal: From Changshan eastward, defending officials either abandoned cities and fled, or bowed forehead at the army gate; only Zhongshan, Ye, and Xindu three cities did not submit.
idiomatic: East of Changshan, magistrates either fled or came to surrender; only Zhongshan, Ye, and Xindu still held out.

literal: Separate order to Eastern Campaign Grand General Dongping Duke Yi with fifty thousand cavalry south to attack Ye; Champion General Wang Jian, Left Army General Li Li, and others attacked Xindu; where the army passed, they must not harm the people's mulberry trees and jujubes.
idiomatic: He ordered Grand General Yi of Dongping south against Ye with fifty thousand horse, and Wang Jian and Li Li against Xindu, forbidding any harm to mulberry groves along the line of march.

literal: On day wuwu, advanced army to Zhongshan.
idiomatic: On the wuwu day he advanced on Zhongshan.

literal: On day jiwei, led cavalry to besiege it.
idiomatic: On the jiwei day he invested the city with cavalry.

literal: The emperor told the generals: "I reckon Bao cannot come out to battle and is sure to rely on the city to defend himself, stealing extra days and months; urgent attack then injures the soldiers, long defense then wastes grain — better first pacify Ye and Xindu, then return to take Zhongshan; for planning this is convenient.
idiomatic: The emperor told his generals, "Bao will not meet us in the field; he will hide behind the walls and wait us out. A hasty assault wastes men, a long siege wastes grain. Better to take Ye and Xindu first, then return for Zhongshan.

literal: If we shift the army far away, Bao is sure to disperse his masses to seek food among the people; thus people's hearts will part and resist, and attack will be easy to overcome.
idiomatic: If we draw off, he will send his troops to forage among the villages, the people will turn against him, and the city will fall the more easily."

literal: The generals all praised it as good.
idiomatic: His officers agreed.

literal: On day dingmao, the imperial carriage visited Lukou City.
idiomatic: On the dingmao day the court moved to Lukou.

literal: That year, Sima Changming died; his son Dezong presumptuously established himself and sent envoys with court tribute.
idiomatic: That year Sima Changming died; his son Dezong seized the throne and sent tribute envoys.

literal: Lü Guang presumptuously styled himself Heavenly King, era name Great Liang, sent envoys with court tribute.
idiomatic: Lü Guang declared himself Heavenly King of Great Liang and also sent envoys to court.

literal: Year 2, spring, first month, day jihai on the new moon: great feast for the host of ministers at Lukou.
idiomatic: In the second year, on the new moon of the first month of spring, the jihai day, he held a great feast for his ministers at Lukou.

literal: Murong Bao sent his Left Guard General Murong Teng to raid Boling, killing the Zhongshan administrator and the magistrates of Gaoyang counties, plundering tax grain transport.
idiomatic: Murong Bao sent Murong Teng to strike Boling, kill the Zhongshan administrator and several Gaoyang magistrates, and seize tax grain.

literal: At that time Xindu had not yet fallen; on day gengshen, then advanced the army.
idiomatic: Xindu still held out; on the gengshen day he marched against it.

literal: On day renxu, led cavalry to besiege it.
idiomatic: On the renxu day he besieged it with cavalry.

literal: That night, Bao's Jizhou inspector Prince of Yidu Murong Feng crossed the wall and fled, returning to Zhongshan.
idiomatic: That night Murong Feng, Bao's inspector of Jizhou and prince of Yidu, fled over the wall back to Zhongshan.

literal: On day guihai, Bao's Assistant State General Zhang Nang and Protecting Army General Xu Chao led officers and clerks and below to raise the city in surrender.
idiomatic: On the guihai day Zhang Nang and Xu Chao, Bao's generals, surrendered the city with all their officers.

literal: Bao heard the emperor was visiting Xindu, then hurried to Shenze in Boling, encamped at the Hutuo River, sent his younger brother Helin to raid Yangcheng, killing more than three hundred Changshan garrison troops.
idiomatic: Learning that the emperor was at Xindu, Bao rushed to Shenze on the Hutuo, sent his brother Helin against Yangcheng, and killed more than three hundred Changshan defenders.

literal: Bao brought out all treasures and palace women to recruit commanderies and counties; many bandits and ruffians responded.
idiomatic: Bao emptied his treasury and sent out palace women to raise levies; ruffians and outlaws flocked to him.

literal: Second month, day jisi: the emperor advanced and visited Yangcheng.
idiomatic: On the jisi day of the second month the emperor advanced to Yangcheng.

literal: On day dingchou, army at Baixi Mound in Julu, overlooking the Hutuo River.
idiomatic: On the dingchou day he encamped at Baixi Mound in Julu, facing the Hutuo.

literal: That night, Bao led his entire host to attack the camp; fire reached the traveling palace; soldiers and men panicked and scattered.
idiomatic: That night Bao attacked with his whole army; fire reached the imperial quarters and the troops broke in panic.

literal: The emperor startled awake, had no time for cap and clothes, barefoot went out and beat the drum.
idiomatic: The emperor leaped up barefoot, without cap or robe, and beat the alarm drum.

literal: Before long attendants left and right and central army officers and soldiers gradually came to assemble.
idiomatic: Soon his guards and the central army gathered around him.

literal: The emperor set a stratagem formation, arrayed beacon fires outside the camp, released cavalry to charge them; Bao's masses were greatly defeated, beheaded more than ten thousand, captured their generals Gao Chang and others more than four thousand persons.
idiomatic: He formed an ambush, lit beacons outside the camp, and charged with cavalry. Bao's army was shattered; more than ten thousand were killed and four thousand taken, including the general Gao Chang.

literal: On day wuyin, Bao fled to Zhongshan; obtained their weapons, baggage, and stores reckoned at several hundred thousand.
idiomatic: On the wuyin day Bao fled to Zhongshan, leaving arms and baggage in the hundreds of thousands.

literal: Bao's Secretariat Director Min Liang, Secretariat Supervisor Cui Huang, Chamberlain for Ceremonials Sun Yi, Palace Attendant Censor Meng Fu, and others all surrendered.
idiomatic: Min Liang, Cui Huang, Sun Yi, Meng Fu, and other officers of Bao's court surrendered.

literal: Surrenderers followed one after another; bestowed offices and ranks each according to merit.
idiomatic: Surrenders poured in, and each man was rewarded with office and rank.

literal: Xu Chao of Pingyuan gathered masses in revolt at Pancheng; ordered General Xi Ru to capture and behead him.
idiomatic: Xu Chao of Pingyuan rose at Pancheng; General Xi Ru was sent to capture and execute him.

literal: Bingzhou defending general Feng Zhen led his tribe and together with Tujie made rebellion, intending to attack Regional Inspector Yuan Yan; Yan attacked and pacified them.
idiomatic: Feng Zhen of Bingzhou rebelled with his tribe and the Tujie, planning to strike the inspector Yuan Yan, who defeated and pacified them.

literal: At that time, from the battle at Baixi distant and near rumors spread; Helan division chief Fuli Juan, Hetulin division chief Niwuni, Hexi division chief Chinu Gen gathered parties in revolt at Yinyang; Prince of Nan'an Yuan Shun led army to attack them, could not overcome, dead numbered several thousand.
idiomatic: After Baixi, tribes rose in the north: Fuli Juan of the Helan, Niwuni of the Hetulin, and Chinu Gen of the Hexi rebelled at Yinyang. Prince Yuan Shun of Nan'an attacked them but failed, losing thousands of men.

literal: Ordered Pacifying the Distance General Yu Yue to command ten thousand cavalry, return to attack Chinu Gen and others, and destroy them.
idiomatic: Yu Yue was ordered back with ten thousand horse; he destroyed Chinu Gen and his allies.

literal: Third month, day jiyou: the imperial carriage halted at Lunu.
idiomatic: On the jiyou day of the third month the court halted at Lunu.

literal: Bao sent envoys seeking peace, requesting to send Yuan Gu, cede west of Changshan to serve the state, beg to hold east of Zhongshan; the emperor agreed.
idiomatic: Bao sued for peace, offering to return Yuan Gu, cede everything west of Changshan, and keep only the country east of Zhongshan; the emperor agreed.

literal: Before long Bao broke the agreement.
idiomatic: Bao soon broke the truce.

literal: On day xinhai, the imperial carriage halted at Zhongshan, ordered the generals to besiege it.
idiomatic: On the xinhai day he invested Zhongshan.

literal: That night, Bao's younger brother Helin led wife and children and fled to Western Mountain.
idiomatic: That night Bao's brother Helin fled west into the hills with his family.

literal: Bao saw Helin flee, feared he would first seize Helong; on the night of day renzi, then led his wife and children and brothers and clansmen several thousand cavalry north in flight.
idiomatic: Fearing Helin would seize Helong first, Bao fled north on the renzi night with his family and several thousand kin.

literal: Bao's generals Li Shen, Wang Ciduo, Zhang Chao, Jia Gui, and others came to surrender.
idiomatic: Li Shen, Wang Ciduo, Zhang Chao, Jia Gui, and other of Bao's generals submitted.

literal: Sent General Zhangsun Fei in pursuit; reached Fanyang, could not catch up and returned.
idiomatic: Zhangsun Fei pursued as far as Fanyang but could not overtake him and turned back.

literal: Within the city together established Murong Pulins as lord.
idiomatic: The city set up Murong Pulins as its ruler.

literal: Summer, fourth month: the emperor because army grain had not yet arrived, then ordered Eastern Campaign Grand General Dongping Prince Yuan Yi to lift the siege of Ye, move camp to Julu, accumulate rent at Yangcheng.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, with supplies still short, he ordered Prince Yuan Yi of Dongping to raise the siege of Ye, move to Julu, and gather grain at Yangcheng.

literal: Pulins sent out infantry more than six thousand men, watching for openings to attack various encampments; ordered General Zhangsun Fei and others with light cavalry to provoke them; the emperor with Tiger Corps five thousand cut off their rear, beheaded five thousand, captured alive seven hundred, pardoned and released them.
idiomatic: Pulins sent out more than six thousand foot to harass the camps. Zhangsun Fei provoked them with light horse; the emperor's Tiger Guard of five thousand cut off their retreat, killed five thousand, took seven hundred alive, and let them go.

literal: Summer, fifth month, day gengzi: great reward for meritorious ministers.
idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the fifth month of summer he rewarded his great ministers.

literal: The emperor because within Zhongshan city they were coerced by Pulins, while the great army pressed them, wishing to surrender but with no road, therefore secretly sent summons and persuasion.
idiomatic: Knowing the people of Zhongshan were held hostage by Pulins yet longed to yield, he sent secret appeals to them.

literal: On day jiachen, displayed troops to show might to those within the city, ordered all armies to lift siege and move south to await their change.
idiomatic: On the jiachen day he paraded his host before the walls, then drew the armies south to wait for the city to turn.

literal: On day jiayin, appointed Dongping Prince Yuan Yi as Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs, Governor of the Six Provinces Yan, Yu, Yong, Jing, Xu, and Yang, Left Chancellor, enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.
idiomatic: On the jiayin day he made Prince Yuan Yi of Dongping Grand General of Agile Cavalry, supreme commander, governor of six provinces, left chancellor, and prince of Wei.

literal: Prince of Xiangcheng Yuan Ti advanced enfeoffment to prince.
idiomatic: Yuan Ti of Xiangcheng was raised to princely rank.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: Pulins sent Wuhuan Zhang Nang leading more than five thousand men out of the city to seek food, raiding Lingshou in Changshan, killing officials and people.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Pulins sent the Wuhuan Zhang Nang with more than five thousand men out to forage; they ravaged Lingshou in Changshan and killed officials and civilians.

literal: Helin from among the Dingling entered Zhang Nang's army; relying on his masses, again entered Zhongshan, killed Pulins and established himself.
idiomatic: Helin joined Zhang Nang from the Dingling tribes, re-entered Zhongshan, killed Pulins, and declared himself ruler.

literal: The emperor returned and visited Lukou, sent General Zhangsun Fei with one thousand cavalry to raid Zhongshan, entered the outer wall and returned.
idiomatic: The emperor returned to Lukou and sent Zhangsun Fei with a thousand horse to strike Zhongshan, enter the outer wall, and withdraw.

literal: Eighth month, day bingyin on the new moon: the emperor from Lukou advanced army to Jiumen in Changshan.
idiomatic: On the new moon of the eighth month, the bingyin day, he marched from Lukou to Jiumen in Changshan.

literal: At that time great pestilence; men, horses, and cattle mostly died.
idiomatic: A great pestilence swept the army; men, horses, and cattle died in masses.

literal: The emperor asked the generals about the pestilence; they replied: "Of those who remain, barely fourteen or fifteen in a hundred.
idiomatic: He asked his officers how many still stood fit for duty; they said barely one man in seven remained.

literal: At that time Zhongshan still resisted defense, while famine and pestilence both arrived; the host below all thought of returning north.
idiomatic: Zhongshan still held out, famine and plague together afflicted the host, and every officer wished to march north.

literal: The emperor knew their intent, therefore told them: "This is indeed Heaven's mandate — what can be done about it!
idiomatic: Reading their minds, he said, "This is Heaven's will — what is there to do?

literal: All men under the four seas can together become the state; in my manner of comforting them lies the answer — why worry about having no people!
idiomatic: All under heaven may be made into a realm; it is for me to win them — why fear an empty land!"

literal: The host of ministers then did not dare speak again.
idiomatic: No one dared speak of retreat again.

literal: Sent Pacifying the Army Grand General Lueyang Prince Yuan Zun to raid Zhongshan, mowed their grain and fodder, entered the outer wall and returned.
idiomatic: He sent Prince Yuan Zun of Lueyang to cut Zhongshan's crops, enter the outer wall, and return.

literal: Ninth month: Helin hungry and destitute, led more than thirty thousand men out to raid Xinshi.
idiomatic: In the ninth month Helin, starving, led more than thirty thousand men against Xinshi.

literal: On day jiazi at month's end, the emperor advanced army to attack them; Grand Astrologer Chao Chong memorialized saying: "Not auspicious.
idiomatic: On the last day of the month, the jiazi day, he marched to meet them; the Grand Astrologer Chao Chong warned that the day was ill-omened.

literal: " The emperor said: "What is the meaning?
idiomatic: The emperor asked what he meant.

literal: " They replied: "Formerly Zhou of Shang perished on jiazi; military families taboo it.
idiomatic: Chong said, "King Zhou of Shang fell on a jiazi day; soldiers have long feared that date."

literal: " The emperor said: "Zhou of Shang perished on jiazi — did King Wu of Zhou not win on jiazi?
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Zhou fell on jiazi — did King Wu of Zhou not win on jiazi?"

literal: " Chong had nothing to reply.
idiomatic: Chong had no answer.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day bingyin: the emperor advanced army to Xinshi; Helin retreated to block the Fushui, relied on the Jianru marshes to secure himself.
idiomatic: On the bingyin day of the tenth month of winter he advanced on Xinshi. Helin fell back to the Fushui and entrenched in the Jianru marshes.

literal: On day jiaxu, the emperor approached their camp, battled at Yitai Mound, greatly defeated them, beheaded more than nine thousand.
idiomatic: On the jiaxu day he assaulted their camp at Yitai Mound, killed more than nine thousand, and won a crushing victory.

literal: Helin alone on horse fled to Western Mountain, then fled to Ye; Murong De killed him.
idiomatic: Helin fled alone into the western hills, then to Ye, where Murong De killed him.

literal: On day jiashen, those he had appointed as dukes and ministers, Secretariat, generals, officers, and soldiers who surrendered numbered more than twenty thousand.
idiomatic: On the jiashen day more than twenty thousand of his appointed officials, generals, and soldiers surrendered.

literal: His generals Zhang Nang, Li Shen, Murong Wen, and others had earlier come to surrender, soon all fled back; that day captured them again, all pardoned and not questioned.
idiomatic: Zhang Nang, Li Shen, Murong Wen, and others who had surrendered and fled were taken again that day and pardoned without punishment.

literal: Obtained the imperial seal and cord, documents, treasuries, and precious things they transmitted, registered in lists of tens of thousands.
idiomatic: He seized the imperial seal and cord, the archives, the treasury, and treasure beyond counting.

literal: Distributed rewards to meritorious ministers and officers and soldiers each according to rank.
idiomatic: He rewarded ministers and soldiers according to merit.

literal: Zhongshan pacified.
idiomatic: Zhongshan was pacified.

literal: On day yiyou, Prince of Xiangcheng Ti died.
idiomatic: On the yiyou day Prince Yuan Ti of Xiangcheng died.

literal: On day dinghai, sent thirty thousand cavalry to join Prince of Wei Yi, intending to attack Ye.
idiomatic: On the dinghai day he sent thirty thousand horse to Prince Yi of Wei for the assault on Ye.

literal: That year, Xianbei Tufa Wugu privately styled himself Great Chanyu, Prince of Xiping.
idiomatic: That year the Xianbei leader Tufa Wugu took the titles Great Chanyu and Prince of Xiping.

literal: Tianxing year 1, spring, first month: Murong De fled to hold Huatai; Yi captured Ye and collected its granaries.
idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxing, in the first month of spring, Murong De withdrew to Huatai; Yi took Ye and its granaries.

literal: Ordered reward for officers and soldiers each according to merit.
idiomatic: He ordered rewards for the officers and men.

literal: Yi pursued De to the river, could not catch up and returned.
idiomatic: Yi pursued De to the river but could not overtake him and turned back.

literal: On day gengzi, the imperial carriage from Zhongshan traveled to Zhending in Changshan, halted at Gaoyi in Zhao commandery, then visited Ye.
idiomatic: On the gengzi day the court went from Zhongshan to Zhending in Changshan, halted at Gaoyi in Zhao, and then entered Ye.

literal: For people who were old and could not support themselves, ordered commanderies and counties to relieve and succor them.
idiomatic: He ordered the commanderies to succor the aged who could not support themselves.

literal: The emperor reached Ye, toured ascending terraces and towers, viewed throughout the palace city, intending to fix the capital there.
idiomatic: At Ye he climbed the terraces, surveyed the palace, and considered making it his capital.

literal: Thereupon established a traveling secretariat; appointed Dragon Cavalry General Prince of Rinan He Ba as Secretariat Director, with Left Assistant Jia Yi leading clerks and soldiers five thousand men to garrison Ye.
idiomatic: He set up a traveling secretariat, named Prince He Ba of Rinan director, and left Jia Yi with five thousand clerks and troops to hold Ye.

literal: The imperial carriage from Ye returned to Zhongshan; where it passed, inquired after and comforted the people.
idiomatic: Returning from Ye to Zhongshan, he inquired after the people along the route.

literal: Ordered the commanderies and prefectures the great army passed through to remit tax one year, exempted half the rent and levies of the people east of the mountains.
idiomatic: He remitted one year's taxes in every district the army had crossed and halved the levies east of the mountains.

literal: The eastern journey about to return north, mobilized ten thousand men to repair the straight road, from Wangdu Iron Pass chiseled through Heng Ridge to Dai more than five hundred li.
idiomatic: Preparing to march north, he set ten thousand men to cut a straight road from Wangdu through Heng Ridge to Dai, more than five hundred li.

literal: The emperor feared after returning that east of the mountains there would be trouble, therefore established a traveling secretariat at Zhongshan, ordered Left Chancellor, Guardian Secretariat Director, Prince of Wei Yi to garrison Zhongshan, Pacifying the Army Grand General Lueyang Prince Yuan Zun to garrison He Pass in Bohai.
idiomatic: Fearing trouble in the east after his departure, he left a traveling secretariat at Zhongshan under Prince Yi of Wei and stationed Prince Yuan Zun of Lueyang at He Pass in Bohai.

literal: Right Army General Yin Guo earlier supervised rent in Jizhou; hearing the emperor would return, plotted rebellion, intended to raid Xindu; Pacifying the South General Zhangsun Song arrested and sent him, beheaded.
idiomatic: Yin Guo, who had been collecting rent in Jizhou, plotted rebellion when he heard the emperor was leaving; Zhangsun Song seized and executed him.

literal: On day xinyou, the imperial carriage set out from Zhongshan, reaching Yaoshan in Wangdu.
idiomatic: On the xinyou day the court left Zhongshan for Yaoshan in Wangdu.

literal: Relocated the people, officials, and clerks of the six provinces east of the mountains and Tujie, Gaoli, and various Yi thirty-six myriads, artisans and craftsmen more than one hundred thousand mouths, to fill the capital.
idiomatic: He moved three hundred and sixty thousand families from the six eastern provinces, together with Tujie, Koguryo, and other tribes, and more than a hundred thousand artisans, to fill the capital.

literal: [9] The imperial carriage halted at the south of Heng Mountain.
idiomatic: [9] The court halted south of Heng Mountain.

literal: Boling, Bohai, and Zhangwu bandits all rose; Lueyang Prince Yuan Zun and others attacked and pacified them.
idiomatic: Bandits rose in Boling, Bohai, and Zhangwu; Yuan Zun and others suppressed them.

literal: Guangchuan Administrator He Lu killed Jizhou Regional Inspector Wang Fu, drove and compelled garrison troops, plundered Yangping and Dunqiu commanderies, then south crossed the river, fled to Murong De.
idiomatic: He Lu, administrator of Guangchuan, killed the inspector Wang Fu, pressed the garrisons into revolt, raided Yangping and Dunqiu, crossed the river south, and fled to Murong De.

literal: Second month: the imperial carriage from Zhongshan visited Fanchi Palace, again selected garrison guards.
idiomatic: In the second month the court went from Zhongshan to Fanchi Palace and reorganized the palace guard.

literal: Ordered giving newly settled inner migrants plow oxen, calculating mouths to receive fields.
idiomatic: He ordered plow oxen given to the newly resettled colonists and land allotted by household.

literal: Third month: Lishi Hu chief Huyan Tie, Xihe Hu chief Zhang Chong, and others gathered parties of several thousand in rebellion; ordered Pacifying the Distance General Yu Yue to attack and pacify them.
idiomatic: In the third month Huyan Tie of Lishi and Zhang Chong of Xihe rebelled with thousands of followers; Yu Yue was sent to crush them.

literal: Yuyang bandit Kuluguan Tao gathered masses in revolt.
idiomatic: Kuluguan Tao of Yuyang raised a bandit host.
